name: Balint Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Balint Syndrome

criteria.description: Inability to perceive more than one object at a time (simultanagnosia)
Impaired visually guided reaching and hand-eye coordination (optic ataxia)
Difficulty in voluntary eye movements and gaze shifting (ocular apraxia)
Evidence of bilateral parietal-occipital lobe lesions on neuroimaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (simultanagnosia, optic ataxia, ocular apraxia)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by neuroimaging demonstrating bilateral parietal-occipital lesions.

pathognomonic.notes: Inability to perceive multiple objects simultaneously.
Difficulty in voluntary saccadic eye movements.

common.notes: Difficulty in spatial localization and navigation.
Difficulty coordinating visual input with motor output.
Impaired ability to scan visual scenes.
Difficulty in drawing or assembling objects.

occasional.notes: Reduced awareness of one side of visual field.
Inability to read despite preserved writing ability.
searchTerms: unable to read but can write

rare.notes: Occasional perception of unreal visual stimuli.
Mild cognitive deficits beyond visual processing.

imaging: Bilateral parietal-occipital lobe lesions on MRI or CT
Hypometabolism in parietal-occipital regions on PET scan
other: Clinical observation of simultanagnosia, optic ataxia, and ocular apraxia

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive neurodegeneration with prominent visuospatial deficits
More widespread cortical atrophy beyond parietal-occipital regions
Visual field defect limited to one half of visual field
Absence of simultanagnosia and optic ataxia
Primary visual loss due to optic nerve damage
No visuomotor coordination deficits or ocular apraxia

redFlags: Sudden onset of visual and visuomotor deficits
Presence of additional neurological deficits such as hemiparesis or aphasia
references: Rizzo M, Vecera SP. Balint's syndrome and visual attention. Neurology. 2002.
Karnath HO, Ferber S, Himmelbach M. Spatial awareness is a function of the temporal not the posterior parietal lobe. Nature. 2001.
Josephs KA. Posterior cortical atrophy: clinical characteristics and differential diagnosis. Lancet Neurol. 2012.
